report.tagline: A UK online-only fashion store for people in their twenties, selling its own labels and hundreds of other brands.
report.simpleSummary: ASOS is a big online clothes shop from London, aimed at people aged about 18 to 30. It sells its own brands like ASOS Design and Topshop, plus brands like Nike and Levi's. It has no shops: you order online, try at home, and send back what does not fit. After years of losses it made a small profit again in 2026.

overview.whatItDoes: ASOS sells clothes, shoes, beauty and accessories online to young adults. It mixes its own brands with partner brands. Its turnaround plan has been to hold less stock, cut discounts and focus on higher-margin own labels.
howItWorks: Shoppers browse about 50,000 or more products on the app, filtering by size, style and brand.
ASOS Design, Topshop, Topman, Collusion and other own brands are designed in London and made by suppliers.
Partner brands either sell stock to ASOS, or ship it through ASOS's 'Partner Fulfils' model where ASOS takes a commission.
Test and React: ASOS buys small first runs of some items and reorders winners, copying the speed of Shein.
Orders ship from big warehouses in Barnsley (UK) and Berlin; ASOS Premier gives a year of free next-day delivery.
Customers return what does not fit; returns under a minimum basket in the UK carry a fee.
overview.valueProposition: A huge range of on-trend clothes in many sizes, from both ASOS's own labels and big brands, delivered fast with easy returns.

businessModel.summary: ASOS buys or makes clothes and sells them online at a markup. Own labels earn more per item than partner brands. Its profit depends on selling at full price and keeping returns and delivery costs low.

revenueStreams.detail: ASOS Design, Topshop, Topman and others at higher margins.
Brands like Nike and Adidas, bought wholesale or on commission.
Yearly Premier subscriptions and paid delivery.
Brands pay for placement and campaigns on the site.
UK customers pay a fee on returns from low-value orders.

businessModel.pricing: Most own-label items are £10 to £60. Free standard UK delivery on orders over a minimum; ASOS Premier costs about £15 to £20 a year for unlimited next-day delivery. A return fee of about £3.95 applies to UK orders under £40.
costDrivers: Returns handling, since young fashion shoppers return a large share of items
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a £60 UK order, ASOS earns about £28 in gross margin if sold near full price. Picking, packing and delivery cost about £7 to £8. If the customer returns one £20 item, ASOS loses that sale and pays about £3 to £4 to handle the return. Marketing for that order is about £3 to £5. So ASOS keeps maybe £5 to £10 per order before overheads, which is why cutting returns and discounts drove the FY26 profit.

howTheyGetUsers: Instagram and TikTok content and influencers
Partnerships with big brands like Nike
growth.moat: ASOS's moat is weaker than before. It has a strong brand with UK young adults, big data on fit and returns, and own brands like Topshop. But Shein and Zalando can match range and price, so ASOS must win on curation and fit.

pmLessons: Growth at any cost can backfire. ASOS grew with discounts, then had to shrink to become profitable.
Returns are a hidden cost in online fashion. Features that improve fit can matter more than new features.
A test-and-react supply chain can cut unsold stock, even for an established company.
When a cheaper rival appears, compete on what they lack, like brands, quality and speed.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you cut ASOS's return rate without hurting sales?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find return reasons. Ideas: fit tools, better photos, return fees. Track return rate and conversion together.

interviewQuestions.question: Should ASOS charge for all returns?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh lower costs against lost customers. Test in segments. Watch repeat purchase and satisfaction.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you win back young shoppers from Shein?
interviewQuestions.hint: Pick a segment. Compete on quality, brands, speed or style. Propose 2 ideas and metrics.

interviewQuestions.question: What metric would you use for ASOS Premier?
interviewQuestions.hint: Value to users: orders per member, renewal rate. Guardrail: delivery cost per order.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature to help plus-size shoppers.
interviewQuestions.hint: Understand pains: range, fit, images. Ideas: models in many sizes, fit reviews. Measure conversion and returns.
